product.ta-m32.summary: System M32 brought multiuser office work to a modular workstation running TANIX.
product.ta-m32.history: ISER holds a 1985 M32 and attributes its development to Triumph-Adler with help from Microlab. It identifies it as a successor to the BITSY word processor.
product.ta-m32.technical.configuration: TANIX supported multiple workstations and tasks. The manual describes it as an extension of XENIX 3.0 and lists disk, tape and Ergonet networking options.
product.ta-m32.technical.verified: BluMach has no runnable profile for this model.
product.ta-m32.technical.limitations: Model-specific firmware and startup verification remain pending.
